name: People's Democratic Republic of Yemen
native: جمهورية اليمن الديمقراطية الشعبية (Jumhūriyyat al-Yaman ad-Dīmuqrāṭiyya ash-Shaʿbiyya)

predecessors.name: Federation of South Arabia
predecessors.text: the Federation of South Arabia, one of the two British-protected states the National Liberation Front overthrew on 30 November 1967

predecessors.name: Protectorate of South Arabia
predecessors.text: the Protectorate of South Arabia, the second predecessor named in the infobox

successors.name: Republic of Yemen
successors.text: all of South Yemen, which 'unified with the Yemen Arab Republic, on 22 May 1990, to form the present-day Republic of Yemen'

ledger.x: 30 November 1967: the People's Republic of Southern Yemen is proclaimed at Aden.
30 November 1970: the state becomes the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen.
22 May 1990: South Yemen unites with North Yemen.
22 May 1990: the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen ends in the Republic of Yemen (same sentence); its land and North Yemen's make the new state, which Cliopatria draws from 1990.

wars.name: Dhofar Rebellion
wars.outcome: After the leadership change of 1969 the PDRY 'declared support for the Dhofar Revolution' and in 1975 gave 'artillery support against the Omani government'; the page gives no territorial result.

wars.name: North Yemen-South Yemen fighting of 1972
wars.outcome: 'Fighting broke out in 1972, and the short-lived conflict was resolved with negotiations'; North Yemen seized Kamaran in 1972.

wars.name: Second Yemenite War
wars.outcome: Plans for unity were 'put on hold in 1979, as the PDRY funded Red rebels in the YAR'; an Arab League intervention ended the war.

wars.name: South Yemen Civil War
wars.outcome: The civil war began in Aden on 13 January 1986, 'lasted for more than a month and resulted in thousands of casualties'; Ali Nasir Muhammad was ousted and Ali Salem al-Beidh became General Secretary of the Yemeni Socialist Party.

certainty.note: Judgment, not read from a page: the frontiers with Saudi Arabia and Oman ran through desert and were not demarcated in these years; the page describes no frontier treaty.
